content:
Hello, I have been working on a Lean formalization of combinatorial species with Anders Claesson at the University of Iceland (as part of the Iceproof project), and we would like to know if there is interest in having some of this work in Mathlib. The repository is publicly available on Github.

This project is a work in progress that currently includes:

  • The core definitions (species, exponential/type generating series, cycle index series)
  • Classical species (linear orders, cycles, sets, permutations, singletons, unit, zero, powersets)
  • Operations on species (sum, product, cartesian product, composition, derivative, pointing)
  • Algebraic laws: the sum and product form a commutative rig up to isomorphism (though mulAssoc and mulComm are being upgraded from bijections to natural isomorphisms), and the derivative satisfies the sum and Leibniz rules
  • Some series associated with specific species or operations, and identities such as "the derivative of a cycle is a linear order"
  • A computable extension with enumeration functions (making it possible to enumerate all linear orders using labels in Fin 10, for instance)

As far as I can tell, Mathlib has no species support yet (pointers welcome!). I expect the main friction point to be that Mathlib would favor Joyal's categorical definition over the combinatorial presentation of Bergeron, Labelle and Leroux that we followed (though we have a bridge to the categorical one in Species/Categorical.lean). The computable layer is out of Mathlib's scope, but it can simply be left out.

Our questions are:

  • Are combinatorial species a good fit for Mathlib?
  • If so, what part of the field deserves coverage? What would be a reasonable first PR?

We would be happy to discuss that here or in a call. Thank you!
I suspect he may see this anyhow, but when I was trying to learn a bit about combinatorial species I recall @Bhavik Mehta having some opinions here.
